title: Zac Taylor Press Conference - November 25
text: [music] >> All right, go ahead. >> Zach, what did you What were your biggest takeaways watching the film on from Monday? >> Well, disappointed that we were unable to find the win. I think there's a lot of um areas in both phases that we could have been cleaner on that would have given us better opportunity. We didn't take advantage of it. And so now we got to quickly move forward and and we got a big test this week here at home. >> What about uh a lot of conversation about the last minute, of course, and the run versus the pass, putting the ball in Joe's hand, not How do you When you watch the film, did any of your feelings about the way you approached that change? >> mean, it it played out the same either way, and I understand that was because of an injury timeout. But the point is I wanted to kick a field goal with 3 seconds left and win the game um so that you don't give them any opportunity to do what they just did. And so uh again, sometimes it can be different depending on the opponent, depending on the situation, but um I feel very strongly about put the ball in our hands and throw the ball and and see if we can get the first down and win it that way. >> What was your view of the third down sack? >> Um I could have given us a better opportunity there. That that's all I feel about it. >> It looked like a shot play or you talking maybe >> Yeah. I I I Again, it's um it's a tough situation that zeroed us there, uh which we expected, and I think I can give us a better opportunity. >> How's Dalton? >> He'll be day to day. So we 'll see. Um just talked to him this morning and we'll just take it day to day and see where he ends up on Sunday. Today's a walk through only day, so I wouldn't read too much into how he looks today. >> Coach talked about like Jayden Daniels is a very elusive quarterback. He actually would run the ball probably more. What do you look at in terms of the difference between those two? Are they pretty much similar in terms of >> about Tyler and and >> Charlie Sharp yeah, in Orleans. >> Yeah, he'll he'll run. Um he's he's athletic. Um so I give him there. He's made some plays with his legs and um impressed. You know, I I hadn't I studied him a little bit in the draft. We didn't have a lot of crossover taped to to see him before showing up more this year with some of the teams we're playing. Really impressed. You know, they do a lot of draw back and early down similar to us and he's done a really good job finding completions, being accurate, looks very comfortable in the pocket, can make some plays with his feet when he needs to. Um I don't know how young he is, so I hate to call him a young quarterback cuz I'm sure these guys coming out are, you know, closer to my age, but um he's he's done a great job here in U two and and I'm impressed with him. >> How do you feel about where the run game's at after a tough game on >> Well, I I think anytime you look at that and and we need more out of it and that's not an indictment on the running backs. That's not that's that's on everybody, you know, and so um this play caller got to continue to give us more opportunities that are that are good opportunities and we got to make the most of them when we get them. Uh but I think certainly coming out of that game we we need to have more out of the run game. >> And then how much can the screen game be a part of that? It looked like there were some close opportunities. >> Yeah, there there are and they've been hit or miss for us. Um we've had some good ones. We've had some not so good ones and so again we'll continue to evaluate things that that can make our life better there. Good job. >> You've talked about how much you like Colby's mindset >> Mhm. >> You got his first one. >> Yep. >> looked like looked like he was where he was supposed to be, doing what he was supposed to do. >> Yeah. Yeah, he uncovered on that one and got in phase with Joe there on a scramble play. Um I think a little bit exemplifies just kind of where he's at right now just just trying to make plays for us, trying to do his job, trying to be available where he can. And like a lot of guys that have kind of come up in this offense, like you just show us that when you get your opportunity you take advantage of it and I think that was an example of Colby doing that. I think we got a lot of guys right now that are fit that fit that mold. Jack Henry's is in there trying to make opportunities when he gets the ball in his hands and so I've been pleased with those two rookies. You know, I think both those guys have stepped up. >> Joe said post game I think his quote was like we did throw for 300 yards, but what positives did you see offensively this >> Yeah, I think when you start the way it started for us, which is just just a little um you know, we wanted a great flow early on that they kind of have a bad taste in your mouth. We did find a rhythm there for for the middle part of the game. obviously that third and 10 you know we we we they zeroed us um on the second to last drive and and they made a play on us. The play didn't work you know so that that stops that drive and then you finish on the last play with the sack you know again we're zero and that's kind of the the two last third downs is kind of as an offense how you think about how the game ended and you know I put that responsibility on myself you know so um again I think we're still in a great space. We have a tremendous opportunity in front of us. I thought we handled the last three weeks really well. We came out of it two and one and now there's a great opportunity in front of us to get back on the winning track and and I think all of our guys are focused on that. >> Zach how did Brian Cook come out of Sunday's game? >> I think he's sore you know so again he maybe a little limited. I I again I I keep saying don't read too much into today cuz I don't know how it shakes out in the walkthrough if take every rep or not but um he finished the game and so he'll just he'll continue to see how he progresses each day but but right now I feel pretty good about it. >> Coach coming off a game like Washington talk about the value of character of your players. Boy you had a great game but what impressed me was after the game you talked about it's our responsibility why 11 guys have to play better and and just as you adjust to making that um for the New Orleans game it's got to mean a lot to you for him to be in that mindset after his personal success. >> Yeah I think exactly. I think it's very important. People see the big picture and that as a team we got to we got to win the game as a team and lose the game as a team and I think a lot of guys felt that way when we ended the game and um it's a tough league you know it was it was we had a good stretch there two months almost two months without losing a game and then you get one and you remember what losing feels like and it stinks and we don't want to be a part of it anymore and so you want to get back on the track. I'm a little thankful we have a short week so you don't have a lot of time to think about it. Obviously we there's a couple things we got to clean up but um I think it's a great opportunity for us to have a short week get back on the field and and go find ourselves a of and get back in that mindset. >> Thank you. >> Do you >> like you guys need to rotate more on the defensive line after >> You know, yes. But also the first half was very unique in that I think they had a five or six play drive to start and then three and out, three and out, three and out. And then they finished with a six play drive that scored. So those guys felt really good because they were on the sidelines quite a bit. And I think the second half they felt pretty good too. With that being said, you got to find some opportunities for Shamar and Cedric to get in there and mix it in and um it was just a strange first half the way it played. I think in the second half those guys felt really good. Um but but we'll we'll rotate those guys a little more than we have been. >> of Shamar speaking of Shamar, what have you seen from him these last few weeks? >> I I I've been pleased with Shamar. You know, I I know I sound a little bit like a broken record up here and then doesn't take any snaps, so I I get that. But um he's controlling everything he needs to control. He's in a he's in a positive spot right now for us. He's going to provide some opportunity We'll provide him with some opportunity to go make some plays for us and I I like where he's at. So just the way it unfolded last week wasn't wasn't any sort of indictment on him. >> Is he just behind like what why why isn't he getting >> He's right there. You know, it's it's there's four guys that have been in the mix for us and he's one of the four and so that's just where it stands right now. Those two guys that start for us um have played well for us and again that's just the way that the game fell the other day. >> Was there any communication from the league on the illegal formation for Washington's [clears throat] final spike or the one second left on >> Not yet. That'll be later in the week. I I didn't call on it, but though you know, the one second left on the clock, yeah, you'd you'd love to have it. I'm not going to sit here and act like we had some great play that was going to win us the game with one second left. So but we'll we'll get more information that one the week as the week goes here and they they report back. >> If there was an illegal formation, it would not have been a 10 second >> Correct and we actually had covered that on Sunday morning um with our Saturday uh Saturday morning with our team that that exact circumstance um in terms of getting set and the types of run offs that come with those last play of the game situations. So our our players were aware that that was not going to be a 10-second runoff. >> Why was that brought out Saturday morning? Is this something you do every week or was this just a >> Well, we I'll be honest with you, we didn't line up legally against the Steelers and so we had to make sure we covered that and corrected that. It wasn't called, but we were illegal and so we were just making sure Sam Francis was doing a great job making sure our guys knew if you're not moving, then it's not a runoff. If you try to fix it at the last second, it can be a running clock there. So there's there's two differences in how that thing can unfold. so they they they they would it would it would not have benefited us. They would have lost 5 yards obviously, but it wouldn't have benefited us for the clock. >> With the holiday tomorrow, what is is it a a normal workday for you guys or do you do you cut back and give them time with their families >> To Tomorrow is not normal. We just chop off the condensed the day. Normally we have that break between walkthroughs and practice. We eliminate that break and so we just go right into it like we went on a Friday and then we shift the meetings from after practice to Friday. So Friday gets extended a little bit more. We cut them free after practice tomorrow. Um obviously we didn't follow this schedule last year cuz we played on Thanksgiving, but all the years previous we followed it and I felt good about the work we get done. >> With with the way the offense has evolved, how has that affected the evolution of the run game this year? >> Well, I think I think Pitch has said it best. We'll be whoever we need to be as the year goes on. You know, he said that in training camp, said in the offseason. I still feel very strongly about that as the season goes. There's spurts where we can play a certain way. There's there's stretches where we can continue to evolve and lean other directions. Um so I think you'll over over the last half of the season here, we're going to be who we need to be to win each game and if you find a rhythm in an area, sometimes we'll stick with it, sometimes we try to change it up, but um I feel very confident that we have a lot to pull from to where we can find success and that can be majoring in the run game, majoring in the past game, whatever blend it needs to be, I feel very confident that we have the resources to draw on to be who we need to be to win the game. >> Can you given how unique you are with how much you'll pass, what does a good run game look like for y'all in the context of your offense? >> Yeah, efficiency. I'd love to say it's it's constant explosive plays. Um, that hasn't always been the reality. And so oftentimes, and I think a lot of different people can find it different ways, for us it's staying on schedule. When we stay on schedule and we're not living in a second and ten world and a third and long world, which we probably had more third and longs than we've had all season it felt like in this game, and scored 20 points, I think that's that's part of it. We put ourselves in unfavorable situations. And so as an offense, whether it's handing the ball off and being efficient and getting to a second and five or throwing a short pass to get in second and five, it's all the same to me. the run game obviously takes pressure off the linemen. They don't have to pass protect on every single play. Joe doesn't have to make protection calls. So there's obviously advantages there that that we got to continue to lean into and um, that's a large part on me, but um, again it's it's staying on schedule and being being effective has been a a big part of why we're able to score points and be as effective we've been as offense. >> What do you see from New Orleans, I think? >> Good team. You know, it's really talented team. I mean I mean Chase Young stands out immediately. You know, I haven't haven't seen him in a while. He's been a really effective player for my defense. I think they got really good linebackers. Um, really smart team, well coached. Impressed with the quarterback. You know, the more I've gotten to watch him more so in the crossover tape as the season unfolded. [laughter] Um, you know, with Tyson coming back now like he's he's kind of who we thought he was in the draft. Really talented player. Um, so again it's it's a really solid team. I know what their record is, what the record is that that doesn't show up on the tape to me. It's a team that can come in here and is going to battle and try to do everything they can to win and so we got to be ready to roll. >> What did y'all think of Tyson pre-draft? >> Liked him a lot. Really talented player. >> How strange was the lights being out for as long as they were? >> Second time this happened in three weeks, so just par for the course now. It happens more times than not in the last three weeks. So um, I think at home we'll be in great shape at 1:00 on Sunday. >> You said earlier thankful for a short week. Thanksgiving, are you thankful for anything else? >> Yeah. I I think family's the first thing that comes to mind. Just uh tremendous family. Um you know the kind of way we live in Cincinnati we're thankful for um the community we live in. I think it's is big part of my family and so those are the first things that come to mind. >> A lot of ramifications the game tomorrow night Buffalo Kansas City will that be a a family watch party? >> Uh I'm sure I'm sure it'll be on if football's on when I'm at home I'm sure it'll be on but the beauty is we can focus on ourselves right now and I know we stubbed our toe last week but we still have plenty in front of us that we can control and so as long as we focus on that we'll be in good shape but um yeah I'm I'd be lying to you if I said if football's on TV I'm not going to be watching it when I'm at home. >> You know Kellen Moore for a a long time what's it going to be like to to see him on the other sideline as a head coach? >> Yeah I I guess the first time I've seen it that way I yeah I mean my first interaction with Kellen was interviewing him at the combine when he was a player. I was a first year assistant that God was that green and and uh so it's that that was a long time ago. That was what uh 15 years ago. >> Right. >> Um he's had a tremendous career. Happy for him. Good guy. Um run into him at the the owners meetings a couple times and um obviously he's the opponent this week so I I can't say that I'm going to have any feelings looking across and seeing him on the sideline. >> All right. Thank you all. >> Thanks. >> [music]

title: Thanksgiving Victory - Bills Take Down Chiefs 13-10 | Always Gameday in Buffalo

And obviously it went backwards, so it played in their favor. ends. So many guys we can shout out like um Tyler Bass is the hero, but Joe Andre >> tip tips the ball. >> Tips the ball. Um Greg Dorch with the wherewithal to pick up the ball, scoop it up in the rain. >> Let me stop you on there because I I want people to understand how important that was for Greg Dorch. He absolutely had to feel the ball. Like he had no choice. If they want to win the game, he has to feel the ball. If he doesn't feel the ball, a the clock still runs and you probably have one play left. And guess where that play is? from probably midfield or your side of the field. It's unbelievable because they executed the second goound under the two-minute warning perfectly. The first one was sloppy. Not because of the decision. Well, and not because of like the clock management, but more because of some of the play calling and the decision- making. That was I think the best kick that or remember the Jake Elliott like 59 yard that >> How about the 61 yard he had against Miami? I mean I know it was a little warmer but >> that's what I just said. I was like that I mean the conditions in that one were perfect. Correct. This one was so bad and it was such a clutch kick and it the other one too. Really cool moment for him. >> No doubt about it. Tyler Bass and I will say the entire Bill special teams. I think the issue comes back to the part about going backwards. >> And then uh last question here is just do you see any opportunities uh moving forward improving the roster specifically at receiver at all? >> Uh no I think we're okay there. Yep. Yeah well you can't have that. He's he's a young guy. He's got to continue to grow and but you surely can't have the penalties that he had and nobody knows it better than he does but he's can't do that. You don't play a game. They weren't showing a lot. Um and I know when we first were told that they were reviewing the spot so I didn't even know that we were reviewing the catch um and so um I'll have to look at it after. But uh a big time play from him. >> Patrick, I know it was cold and you sweat all day. Just how tough was it to maintain the ball when it was snapped whether it was shotgun or under center? Was it just a case of just >> It did Yeah, no I just got to you got to be uh you had to be locked in the entire time. You know sometimes you you you've taken I've taken so many snaps from Creed and um especially under center and and kind of just kind of start just relax, I guess you would say. But when you're in the the conditions that you're in, you have to be locked in the entire time and I got to be better there. Um catching that snap at the end of the game didn't give us a chance to kind of get anything going um which ended up causing us to to lose on the field goal there. So um you just got to be locked in. It was a big play at the moment, um but it nothing counts unless you go out there and finish the drive. So I mean it's just you have to go out there and execute. Um you have to go out there and play at a high level and coach trusted me to throw the football. You could tell there were some I didn't throw the way I wanted to. Um and that's why I was so confused at first when they they had 4 seconds cuz I thought they saw me call the timeout and we were at least able to get 9 seconds. Um but I don't know exactly what the the time was, but it was I tried to call it immediately. >> Harrison's been with you guys for a for a long time. You know the red zone struggles he's had this season and then and then tonight, is it is the leader of the room, is tonight the night where you you say something to him? You just let him be like how do you deal with that as a leader? >> No, I mean, I try to have confidence in everybody on the team. Like that that's that's part of playing this sport is believing in the guys around you. Um and obviously Harrison hasn't had the season that he's he's wanted this year, but he's also been one of the best kickers in the game for a long time and I know he's working at it. I can tell you that and he's he's doing his best to be the best teammate that he could be and go out there and execute in those moments um unfortunately tonight it didn't go his way. Um but I I promise you he'll come back and work out it again and and hopefully the next time he'll be able to go out there and and make it happen. >> I think details and being disciplined on all phases of the ball matters. Um I think I jumped offsides tonight. It was cold, it was rain. But it's just like any any any playoff football. You know, you in those type of conditions, whether it's snow, rain, for me it's just about buckling up and going out there and playing. >> How was that footing condition? Was that footing suitable? >> Yeah, it was suitable. Um grass fields um felt really really good and you know, it wasn't as bad as I thought it was going to be, but >> What do you tell the guys the younger guys going into next week? >> Um we got to move forward. We got to move forward. Um [clears throat] most likely we'll see these guys again. It's a lot to learn from overall. Um but we got to move forward. We got a couple days to adjust recalibrate get our get our focus back right, watch a little film, see what we can be better at and continue to move forward. >> What's what's sticking with you right now about this one? >> A lot. A lot, man. A lot. Um this was a tough one. We wanted it so bad. Unfortunately we didn't we wasn't able to pull it off, but um it's a lot we can learn from. It's a lot you know, a lot of positive also. >> These are seem to be the marquee matchups Kansas City Buffalo Bills. Um what can you say about just the resilience of the team despite the penalties uh moving forward is possible for this team? >> Just got to continue to move forward, man. Penalties are part of it. We try to minimize the penalties um the penalties that we can control as much as we can, but it's a part of the game. Um cleaning that up um I think emphasizes on this week cleaning up the penalties and going forward. Some critical penalties uh controversial calls uh in the second half. Even at 10 seven the Chiefs had the ball and they get a big play down to the 17 yard line and Noah Gray and you're thinking if they punch it in here it might be game set match. >> Yeah, it did. >> Uh >> very frustrating all around here in this game, and uh stuff that we could have corrected, stuff that feels unforced uh here in this one, but the reality is it happened. So give him credit, but it's frustrating because it feels like he shouldn't have had that opportunity. It feels like we should have won this game by double digits, honestly. Again though, for our defense, time and time again even after that to step up and give us a chance to win this football game, my hurts for them because they played well enough to win this game. >> Okay. Maybe you've researched this. I haven't. Uh but to go Thursday to Thursday, never seen that. And these are the moments that you learn about the character of your team and and hopefully this is a moment that we're going to learn from and um later on this year we'll look back on and say, hey, our team really found out who they were after that tough loss. >> No question. title: The Vikings CANNOT Get Beat By Bijan Robinson
text: The key for the Vikings to beat the Falcons is quite obvious, but difficult to achieve. Simply don't lose against Bijan Robinson. part of the Locked On podcast network. Your team every day. What's up, everyone?  Welcome to the Locked on Vikings podcast, where we always try to learn something new.  Today on the program we analyze the clash between the Vikings and the Falcons.  I'm recording this on Wednesday, late in the afternoon.  So I have no idea what happened Wednesday night or on Thanksgiving. I'm still learning about the Steelers.  So I don't have any injury reports or anything like that yet because of the early recording, but what I can talk about is Bijan Robinson. This is the key to beating the Falcons, at least on the offensive side of the ball.  We'll talk a little about defense, but I'll focus much more on the Falcons' offense and the Vikings' defense, which is looking to bounce back from Sunday night's disaster against the 49ers. This episode is presented by FanDuel .  Join the NFL action all season long with FanDuel. It starts at fanduel.com. So what's terrifying about Bijan Robinson is more or less what the Vikings experienced last year. That wasn't the main headline of the game against the Falcons, of course , where J.J.  McCarthy played so badly and then injured himself with the ankle sprain, which led to a story that defined the season. But on the other side of the ball, they definitely had some trouble tackling him. And what I really want to talk about is how Bijan Robinson tries to break a tackle. I understand that Bijan is a "jump cutter". There are several styles. There are "cut and go" running backs like Aaron Jones, who aren't going to break a lot of tackles. They are more physical, the kind who runs over an opponent on the goal line . And that's not always what Aaron Jones was, but it's much more about explosiveness and angles than making fakes or using the spin button. Then there are the "spin button " types, who I think are only viable in college, because in the NFL we're too good at tackling to rely solely on spins. And then there are guys like Bijan, who is a "jump cutter". Perhaps the best "jump cutter" of all time was Adrian Peterson.  Being a "jump cutter" can work perfectly, but you have to be really, really good at it.  And that's how the "jump cut" manifests itself. You usually try to take advantage of someone, right? You take an outward angle and that guy follows you outward. You plant one foot on the ground and suddenly start going the other way, which ruins everyone's angles, right? If you imagine a drill, like those you see in Madden, where you have the running back against the whole field and everyone is chasing you, right? Uh, imagine there were no blockers , nothing.  It was just one running back against 11 defenders, and they all started at different points on the field, and you had to dodge them, right?  Let's say you're on one side and everyone starts on the other side, so everyone has to calculate their angle towards you, right? That angle is something that teams practice a lot, taking that angle and trying to improve, but there isn't really a defined technique. It's more a matter of instinct, of knowing what angle to take so as not to overshoot, not to fall short, to make sure you get where you need to go and track the guy's nearby hip so you can reach him and try to make a tackle When you crop and practically teleport yourself 3 yards back , everyone's angle suddenly becomes incorrect. So, what you need to do to avoid this destroying you is to be very good at pincer tackles and you need a lot of players to regroup. This is a struggle for Brian Flores at times, and that's why there's a perception, although I think it's exaggerated, but it has some basis, that a very good runner can take away strength from what Flores does. Because the way their coverage works, specifically the "hot quarters," which is their signature coverage, leaves many players in one-on-one tackle situations. Now you have a guy to tackle the runner, so schematically it's acceptable.  We'll accept it.  Works. But it's a one-on-one.  If you miss that tackle, the consequences can be really serious.  That's where we shouldn't be.  So when I say pincer tackle, I mean two guys, one coming from inside and one from outside, who meet the runner and bring him down cleanly.  So there's no misunderstanding, right?  If I have help on my left and I'm coming from the right, I don't mind if it cuts to the right. That guy is going to make a direct cut towards my teammate.  And vice versa, my partner isn't worried if the runner cuts towards me, because he'll come straight to my area and I'll be able to make the entry. Then, each person can take care of half of the player cleanly and that's it , it's done.  But the key to this is , again, a matter of space, instinct, and consciousness;  It's about being able to get hip to hip with that player and making sure that moment is right in front of the runner so he doesn't run you over. For example, George Kittle's touchdown last week, the first one where he went through Josh Metellus and I think Harrison Smith, they were too far apart.  So none of them actually arrived and they didn't appear at the same time. Then one falls, the other falls, and breaking through an entrance twice is much easier for Kittle, who is bigger than both of them, than if they had both arrived at the same time.  That's the level of precision that will be required here. So that's what they need to get really, really good at this week. If they can get really good at that this week, they can eliminate the threat of the lateral cut. And that's important to be able to reliably tackle Bijan Robinson and take that weapon away from him. That's where I think it's most dangerous and where I'd like to focus a large part of my effort. And, generally speaking, if I were in that defensive room and we had just had a collapse game like this, I would feel very comfortable forgetting about it. But as for the offense, you know, after their fourth meltdown of the year against Buffalo, we haven't forgotten that.  You know, we're holding people accountable and we need to find out what's going on But for the defense, which had nine incredibly good games and just had its first bad one, I would absolutely erase the tape and say that's not who we are;  It was a stroke of luck, we'll move on, right? That is absolutely the mindset I would adopt in this.  And to that end, I don't think the Vikings should spend this week looking for answers on defense and asking themselves: What's wrong with us? What happened ?  We need to solve our own problems.  I think they should forget about it and say: alright, Falcons next, what about Bijan? There is another factor in this. Um, the Falcons...well, I guess I can talk a little bit about what I noticed in the Falcons' ground game. So on patreon.com/lukebraunnfl, I analyzed the Falcons.  I watched their game against the Bears. And in that game against the Bears, it seemed like there was a decent amount of pass production.  It wasn't a great ground game because they were behind on the scoreboard for a long time, but I saw enough to know what I'm seeing and I'm familiar enough with Bijan to know what that threat is.  I mean, he's been in the league for a couple of years now, so that's not something you need to investigate to know what 's going on. So that was the game I chose for that video and it told me a lot, because the Bears in that game used a lot of Flores' stuff. They used all-over presentations, they used non-traditional tapas, they used a lot of those kinds of cuts and twists that the Vikings do up front.  They took many of the concepts from the Vikings, and by the way, that's happening all over the league.  You're starting to see that Flores...Flores brought a lot of interesting ideas that were very destructive and poured them into the league all at once, and everyone who watches a Vikings game or plays against them says, "Oh , we got that." It's bigger than me. We need to keep improving.  We need to keep improving.  And I think we're on the right track. Regarding your case.  I saw the story you made with Greg.  It was great.  What made you feel such passion for veterans? Yes. I visited Camp Hope for the first time last year.   It was like a life-changing moment for me because many veterans sacrifice a lot of time to help this country and then they don't have the resources they need when they return, when they struggle with post-traumatic stress disorder. Camp Hope is also based on faith.  So helping them find faith is something I'm passionate about.  It was great.  And this year I'm going again, and it's like another layer.  They go to this place called Sayer.  I don't know if you can see it.  Yes, this place. It is a place with horses where children with disabilities can ride horses and have an escape route.  But veterans can also connect with horses and learn to build trust.  And sometimes it's as if men are a little stubborn.  So building that trust with the horse and asking for help and knowing that it's okay to ask for help was also great. Perhaps I'm wrong, but it seems to me that , as a defensive player, one of the best things you can do is get a safety.  Do you agree?   I'm not going to lie to you.  That was it...I didn't know I had a safety until I got to the sideline.  Ray said, "Dude, that was a safety." But it's crazy because I thought I had a safety.  I thought I had...I don't know what I thought last year against Seattle. Yes. I don't know what was happening.  I was too excited.  But yeah, I guess it's great.  Although it is a blessing. Was that your first safety? Or did you have one at Alabama? No, it was the first one. The last time I had a safety, Coach Fed went crazy because he texted me, my high school coach. The last time I had a deep sleep was in high school.  So yes. Well, now that you think about the awards, the Defensive Player of the Week award, you also win the Defensive Player of the Year award, the Defensive Rookie of the Year award. When you think back to winning the Lombardi in college and the award that will be announced here in Houston soon, what did it make you think about your childhood and growing up in college? What did that award mean to you? Yes, it meant a lot to me. It's crazy because I always allude to this, but we're talking about safety again. I simply played the way I didn't like, especially at university, because I did n't really like scoring goals at university.  It probably only scored three.  So winning an award like that was really great because you worked so hard .  College football demands a lot.  You have school, tutoring, staying up late, all those things; you have to get up early, train, and work hard. And then you're competing with many more players in the country than in the league.  There are many very good football players. So being recognized with that award was really great and I wish the best to whoever receives it this year. Putting that aside, how do you maintain your appetite?  Because the coach was talking about how you impact the game beyond the scoreboard.  There are many things you do that don't appear there.  How do you maintain your hunger and keep improving? It's strange because there's always something else to do.  There's always something more to achieve.  You always know, when you love something, you keep chasing after it. And the coach put this quote on the board today, which I thought was, you know , just right, but it just said what you think, whatever it is you think, what did it say?   It was like what you think about or something like what matters to you or something like that, you think about it and you go after it.  And I care about football, so every day I'm determined to go after it.  And it's not about chasing a statistic, it's not about chasing, it's only about chasing greatness.  It's like how good you can be at this.  How good can you be at that? And can you be the best at it?  And that's what I always have in mind, like wanting to leave my legacy and be one of the best to ever step onto the field, you know, when all is said and done. When you look at the season and all that , it seems like you guys need to win every week more or less.   Do you feel like the playoffs have already started? Like you're already in that elimination mindset? Yes. I think for us, you know, we can see it that way, but I think right now what we're focusing on is taking things one game at a time Yes, these games are serious, we have to win them all, but I think when you try to get too far ahead and look back at our season, we 're getting ahead of ourselves.   We are seeing something we don't need to see.  We just need to focus on the present.  And the present right now is the Baltimore Ravens.  How can we play in all three phases of complementary American football? And I think that's the most important thing for us right now, the challenge is to get two consecutive and consistent wins this season.  Sorry , you said they weren't statistics .   Have you ever thought about taking 20 screenshots That's the rarest sack season in NFL history.  Have you thought about it? Does it motivate you in any way? Yes, I mean, it's crazy because a lot of people tell me that, but I think that, in my case, I write down all my goals and things like that. Well, but you know, I'm just trying to really learn, to keep letting God use me in a certain way, because I think when you try to strive to achieve things and you really try to achieve them, that's when you get frustrated when you don't achieve something.  So I think when you go into a game trusting in your preparation, trusting in all the hard work you're doing, you never know when it's going to show up.  You never know when you're going to get a catch in a game.  You never know when you're going to get that ticket that will make you lose a game.  But what you can know is that you prepared well for those things to happen.  And for me, when I face each game, of course you have statistics you want, you have goals you want.  But I think the most important thing is to go out and pursue, you know, greatness.  Do you know what I mean?  As long as you pursue greatness, as long as you trust in your ability, I believe all those things will come.  So it will be a blessing if I look up and the season ends and I'm right there with that number.  Do you know what I mean?  So, again, for me the most important thing is to get back out there , have fun, and fly with the guys How much of your motivation is based on the fact that you know many of your players depend on you?  You know that if you do your job to the best of your ability, that will help the linebackers, and in turn , that will help the defensive backs. So, when you go into the game, how much of that do you have in mind? And what does the motivation Greg gave you about the 20 captures have to do with the fact that you have conversations with Miles Garrett and Michael Parsons? Yes. For me, you know, being a leader on this team and I think I'm going back to Demeco.  He does a good job, man, I think he motivates us to play.  But you talk about winning with impact. You know that's something we pride ourselves on in the defensive line, how big of an impact can you have on wins? How are you going to have an impact on wins today?  And for me, individually, it's always a big goal.  How am I going to make an impact today?  Even if I don't get a capture today, how did I perform for my brother? Did I do my job well enough for him? Was I where I needed to be?  Even if he did n't make the move, did he make it So, in my case, we don't talk about all the stats or anything like that, but about whether I gave my best today to have an impact on every play, whether it's by pressing, setting the limit, closing when I need to close, raising my hand and all that kind of stuff. And you know, I'm the little brother, you know what I mean?  And I can't wait to watch this game tonight because it's going to be fun. But hey, those are two guys I have a lot of respect for, Miles and Micah.   I ca n't wait to see them both play You know, it's always a friendly competition, you know what I mean? Friendly fire, but hey, let's keep it that way.  There's not much to say. When you go up against Derek Carr, you go up against him a lot. You need to make him cut off his feet, man .  You have to make him stop.  You can't let it go downhill.   You ca n't let it go, you know, I mean north and south.  You need to be able to make it go east and west.  So I think it's going to be very important for us to establish the edges, close them off, and make sure we 're sticking them body to body, wrapping them up, and bringing them to the ground. The technical aspect of the game that allows you to get closer to the quarterback , were there any specific areas where you feel you've improved and that you 've emphasized this offseason? Yes, I would definitely say that my counterattacks and much better use of my hands.   I also really like it when they put it inside me.  It's been a lot of fun.  I've had the opportunity to learn a lot from Rank about how to run on the inside.  That's one aspect of my game that I want to improve.  I know we tried a little bit in my rookie year and I still struggled, but I think the more I've become the player I am, recognizing my ability and having confidence in it, the more I've been able to use my hands more effectively inside and outside, and counterattack a little better and finish over the quarterback. Facing them last year.  What do you remember about Jacob Brissett and Arizona, and how it hasn't developed? Yes, I must say he's a great runner. He's a great quarterback, man.  Like a dog, it's very subtle.  I think he has one of the best pocket presentations as a quarterback in this league.  I mean, he's very subtle with his movements, just turning the corner.  He takes a step forward, gives you his shoulder, throws deep passes downfield. The four players will have to pressure whoever is charging to knock them down. We have a lot of respect for them, man, like last year the coach showed us a video of all the missed catches we made last year. So we have to do a really good job to finish strong with him this year. When you respect that, how do you stay focused on the game if you don't get a capture and still find other ways to make an impact? That's a great question.   It took me a long, long time to understand it. Rank and D Hunt, a big shout-out to them .  Those two guys, as I said, have kept me grounded.  And I think once I learned that, you know, you have this fairy tale in your head that you're going to get a sack in every game, and the reality is that you're not going to get a sack in every game. But again, I think it goes back to what I was saying before.  When you trust in your ability and know that you are being the best version of yourself, whether you get a catch in the game or not, you know who you have, you know your identity, and you know what kind of player you are.  You know you're a great player whether you get a catch in the game or not.  And, once again, you play the game again.  If you're pressured, you 're taking the quarterback out of position.  You've made 12 attempts without a single capture.  Well, he hasn't managed to capture any.  But dude, I took down the quarterback and made him feel uncomfortable.  And you'll probably help someone else get a couple of catches that day too.  I think I look at our defensive line and we have a lot of guys who selflessly rush to help everyone.  And I think one of the most important things is knowing who your identity is and knowing that you are an amazing athlete.  You're an amazing player game or not. It is the follow-up of that will.   Is that the mental aspect of the game where you've learned from Rank and D Hunt so they can tell you that you have all the physical tools to do this job? But now, once you add that mindset, it will take you to the next level. Definitely.  And Rank has been with me since my rookie year and he always tells me how proud he is of me, especially in the mental part of the game. Because there were moments after the game , in my rookie year, man, I was playing in my locker room and Rank was saying to me, "Bro, you're doing everything right ."  It will come.  When it arrives, we'll look up and laugh about those moments.  And then D Hunt said, brother, it's part of it. The captures come in piles and I've seen him take captures in matches without captures and get one out of three, get one out of four.  And it's been like what I used to say, he's like fire , he's like ice.  And every time he sees me stumble or about to achieve something, he tells me, brother, calm down.  Remember who you are.  It will come.  Continue with your process. Keep having fun and everything will be alright.  So I think that, from that point of view, they've been able to help me a lot with my mindset instead of thinking, you know who you are, dude.  Keep trying. Continue with your process and have fun doing it. It's rivalry week in college football.  I just have to ask you, what's your favorite Roll Tide ? What's your favorite Iron Bowl memory and what makes it the best rivalry in college football? My favorite memory from the Iron Bowl is when we played against Auburn in Auburn and Bryce, I think, made a 90- yard run down the field and we ended up winning the game. And for me, I always feel that the Iron Bowl was better when it was played at Auburn because I don't know.  They were doing crazy things there.  We crushed them when we were in Alabama. But I think it's the biggest rivalry because it's a game like Alabama and it has a lot of history. And I'll never forget that coach Saban said: this [ __ ] game means a lot to a lot of people here.  They will remember this match forever.  And I remember that I think they lost and that it hurt them. It hurt them because that's how serious it was.  But you know, when it comes to rivalry games, you can see how much they mean to a lot of people in the state of Alabama.  It's like you either see yourself in red and white or in blue and orange. Although it's more red and white.  So Roll Tide. Thank you all. Thank you. Oh.   Are these mine? I guess... I guess... Why are they here? Oh. Brilliant. The mentality is one game at a time, and that's how it has to be at the start of the season. How do you deal with that every week knowing that the scoreboard is rubbish and it's not going to help you?  The only thing that helps is seeing a victory. Yes, I mean, you can only control what you can.   I know it's like focusing on what's in front of you.  You know, always think about what's in front of you.  You really need to focus on that, like it's the game, you know, like it's a walkthrough of a meeting.  So that's going to be the focus, you know, for us, you know, this week too I forgot to ask you about this other game , but the pass you made to Nico, what were you thinking while you were doing it and how were you able to make that pass?   You weren't really thinking while you were playing.  I mean, when the ball lit up, like... I wouldn't say you weren't thinking, but it's really fast.   I wasn't really thinking about anything specific.   I just saw Nico win, so I was doing everything I could to give him the ball.  He did a good job aiming high with the ball and making a play with it.  So yeah, I was just trying to give him the ball as best I could. Obviously you have a lot of good receivers on this team, but what does it mean to have a guy like Nico who is so reliable and always there for you? Do you feel like you play together that much? Yes, it means a lot.  I love Nico as a friend, as a brother, as a teammate. I love how she is, how hard she's worked since I arrived.   He's doing a great job for us and does a lot of things that aren't reflected in the statistics.  So I have a lot of respect for the leader he is and for what he's been doing these past few years. What do you see in the growth of the offensive line, protecting you, but also opening up some holes, especially in this last game for David Montgomery? Yes, I thought it was great.  I thought we could get a good ground game to make it more balanced .  I think that's good for us. I think we can still be aggressive throwing the ball and I think we've made a lot of money doing that this year. Well, you definitely have to be able to be balanced, but, you know, I definitely love how they told DeMo to be the rock and to bring back Woody. We will definitely help with that too. When you look at Baltimore's defense, what stands out about them?   They may not have lived up to their standard this year, but they still have professional talents like Roquan and Kyle. Yes, they play hard.  They play hard from top to bottom, from the safety to the linebackers, cornerbacks, and defensive linemen. And I think Roquan leads those guys and has a high standard.  And I think Kyle is, if not the best safety, one of the best safeties in the league, and he does a great job.  And I am a big fan of his and what he has been able to do in his career so far. Well, you know, we have to keep an eye on our P and Q, but they play very hard. CJ, who do you represent with your boots and why did you choose that option? I have my base on my boots and I also have another pair of boots that I will use that says "God, God trusts". That simply puts my trust in the Lord.  But also our foundation, my mother has done a great job with that, my family.  We're all in this together .  And we just try to reach as many people as possible and show God's love, the love that God has given us to others, and help them with food , clothing, or whatever. Well, we just want to be a service to others, that's what we stand for and what we try to do on Sunday with the tacos. Jay, we all know you and Will get along well, but what do you think about him winning Defensive Player of the Week this week?   I think it's incredible.  I think he's done a great job. I think some of the things that a person who sometimes doesn't appear in the statistics does is receive a lot of attention and help others to break free, so I'm very happy for him and proud of him. I think he is one of the best football players I have ever seen, in my opinion.  And I'm very grateful that he's on my team.  And seeing what a man he has become over the years has been great. In that sense, I know you faced him in practice, but can you imagine if he wasn't your teammate and you had to face him on game day? Yes, I would try to align myself and do the best I could, but I think, God, he's on my team. You mentioned it earlier this season.  What was it like to see the hard work Marlon has put in to get on the same page as you guys, go on offense and contribute, and finally go out and score that touchdown? Yes, it was great to see him.  You know, the young man did a good job and I think he's learning.   He's learning fast and he's very talented.   You just have to put it on the same page as you said, put it on the same page as us in what we're trying to achieve, and whenever it does the right thing, you know, it's usually pretty good. Well, we just have to keep letting him develop and grow, and that depends on our whole team helping him, but he's doing a great job and effort or physicality isn't really the issue.  We simply need to find ways to make sure he's on the same page as everyone else, and he's been able to do that these last two weeks .  I am very, very proud of him and I am a big fan of Marlon and what he has been able to do and continues to do great things for us. Having Marlon back. We talk a lot about the offensive line here .  Can you tell us about some different players who get the opportunity to touch the ball and how that helps you in terms of depth, like when it was Braden Smith this week or last week it was Betchi? What do you see, lads? A young player like Betchi and other players who get the opportunity to play up front? Yes, I think Betchi has been great. You know, I think he's brought a certain tenacity and determination to the offensive line since the camp. I think Keelan has been one of them too.  I think Braden has done the same thing in the ground game.  I think Trent has been playing well too.  So , well, for me it's good, at least, to have some depth there. But I think we need to be able to play elite-level football in all five positions. And I think the more players challenge each other, the better, but I definitely want to get into a rhythm with the players we're going to play with.  So I think Trent has also done very well alongside Braden. I think Braden did very well on Sunday and Thursday, and then we'll continue to see where we stand, but I think it's good to have some depth. So, with Marlon back in practice and getting him used to the offense, what do you think he could do for you guys down the stretch? Yes, I think having him back now is the perfect time for him to get going and he's been doing some great routes.  I think everyone's been watching him, he just has to find ways to get into the rock.  But I think he's doing a great job, you know , creating separation, and we'll continue to do that for ourselves. Speaking of, you know, you're saying you have one, I guess it's your brand , of course, God made it.  Can you explain that a little more? Yes, I mean, I would say that self- confidence is great, but I think that when you, as a believer in Christ, I think we are called to think less of ourselves, but that doesn't mean being too hard on yourself. It's like giving yourself grace, but understanding that God's grace is greater than anything you can do on your own.  So that's what it means to me. But I live by that because sometimes I have days when I'm not the most confident person, but I know that God has put a great talent in me. And even when I cannot be strong, He is strong for me.  Well, I love the verse 1 John 4:4 that says, "Greater is he who is in me than he who is in the world." That gives me a lot of confidence, because you know that the Holy Spirit that is in me is stronger than my carnal being, and even when I am weak, I am strong thanks to who God is in my life. Along the same lines, how are you able , when you're on the field and you have plays you don't like or plays you'd like to recover, how are you able to put that aside and leave it behind when it's time to go in for the next series?   I mean , that's life, you know?  I believe that if someone punches you in the mouth, you have to be able to respond. And one thing that I think people—not just people, but I think sometimes even I forget—is that the other team gets paid too.  They are good opponents.  As if they had a player or two and, well, you know, they might even have a great day.  You never know, but the goal is always to win a game and getting angry about something or thinking badly about yourself or that play isn't going to help. And it took me a long time to get to that point where I was able to say, "Well, that happened, what can I do to like it more and learn from it?" And I've been able to do that a little bit this season. So it's not easy, but you have to be able to do it because nobody cares about your excuses about what happened or what didn't happen. You need to find a way to let it go and move on because I think there are better plays to make. How would you describe the impact of confidence on players in general in any sport? Yes, I believe confidence is almost everything, especially in the NFL.  Like me, I 've seen guys coming out of college who are great players, who were All-Americans or who did this and that in college, and they get to the NFL and sometimes, it can be a coach, an organization or whatever , that can take away the player's confidence. And, unfortunately, it may be because people simply don't know what they're doing, and secondly, it may also be because this person is simply less hungry. But I think that means a lot. You have to be a confident person , because nowadays everyone has an opinion, and rightly so, I think. People are entitled to their own opinions, and it's up to you whether you pay attention to them or not. But, well, I think, you know, who you think you are and who God thinks you are is, ultimately, the most important thing. So, well, I don't really care if you're a coach or not.  But even when you're in the selection process , you'll go to those 30 visits, or some of those visits, and you'll sit in a room with a bunch of coaches and executives and they'll question you about everything you've done in your life. And that can undermine your confidence if you're not a confident person. Well, so in those moments I choose not to really worry, because I know who I am. But, well, you still respect, you know , who they are and what they've done;  But that doesn't mean they're God or like your parents. You can still have self-respect while playing this game at an elite level.   Do you and Nico have a friendly bet planned for Saturday? No. The coach just said he'll ask everyone not to tire their feet tomorrow. What do you enjoy most about Thanksgiving, both the dinner and its meaning? I think Thanksgiving is amazing .  I love Thanksgiving just to be thankful for a lot of different things.   I already talked about that on Thursday and after the game, just about what I was grateful for. But yes, I want to say that I will enjoy it with my family when we finish here. So when I'm here I'll focus on what I have to do and then I'll go home to study a little, but I'll enjoy it with the family and just relax and try to, you know, eat something nice, but not eat too much, but still enjoy myself. I'll find time to relax, but I'll also try to stay focused . What kind of healthy balance have you been able to achieve? Yes, I firmly believe that you can't be playing football all day, every day.  It's like people catch me in random places, sometimes just being a human, and say to me, " What are you doing here?" As if he were a human, as if he were a dog, as if he weren't a banker, as if he weren't thinking about banking all day , as if he were going to the movies or watching films. So it's okay to be a person.  I think that, sometimes, outside noise can make you feel like you're not focused or concentrating just because you enjoy certain things.  And now, I think you could be doing too much and doing too many things, but I don't really have that problem, I don't think so.  But, well, I choose, you know, when I'm with my family or at the movies or doing X, Y or Z , I enjoy every second of it.  And then , when I'm playing or training or in meetings or at the facilities, I'm going to do my best to focus on what I can at that moment or what I need to do for football.  So you have to have a balance, but it's not a bad thing to be human. What dish does your mother or whoever is cooking make that you have to try for Thanksgiving? My mother makes good macaroni and cheese, my sister makes good sweet potatoes. Well, they do...I mean, I like everything.  I tried the filling for the first time yesterday.  The truth is, I liked it.  I had never tried it before.   It seemed strange to me when I was little.  So I didn't know.  But it's normal.   They're going to cut it.  My God.

title: Why Houston Texans are ignoring playoff scenarios and looking inward: laser-focused on Ravens
text: No, we can't celebrate Thanksgiving .  No. I told all our guys at the meeting on Monday that we shouldn't worry about Thanksgiving.  We have much more important things ahead of us. Undoubtedly.  Well, yes.  Like you said, dude, you can't keep looking at the scoreboard.  We have to go out and do our thing, game by game, team by team .  Whatever our job is, we must do it.  And now we have to show our best football. That's the only thing that matters.  I know this is on everyone's lips right now.  There's a lot of talk about the standings, about whether you have this or that chance. Our only chance, in my opinion, under any scenario, is for the Texans to win. So we have to make sure we are collected , focused on preparation, focused on ourselves and doing everything we need to do to go out and play good football. We can look at it that way, but I think right now we're just focusing on each next game.  Of course, these games are serious.  We need to win all these matches , but when you try to look too far ahead, looking back at the season, we are in too much of a hurry.  We look at things we shouldn't look at.  We just need to focus on the present moment.  And now it's the Baltimore Ravens.  How do we go out and show consistent football in all three phases?  And I think the most important thing for us now is to win two consecutive confident victories this season. I guess you can only control what you can control.  I know, you just have to focus on what's in front of you.  I always say: whatever you're focused on, you have to give it your all , as if it were a real game—whether it's a warm-up or a practice.  So that will be our focus this week. Like you said, it's hard not to look ahead, but you have to be where you stand now.  You should be where you are.   We must remember our missions and goals. And, man, you just have to keep doing it .  You know, um, you can't get too distracted by what's going on around you, because you can lose sight of your goal.  You know, but, um, stay hungry, dude.  This is your mood. Stay hungry.  Um, keep the main thing the main thing, man.  Keep moving forward. Hello everyone, Aaron Wilson from Reliant Stadium.  Happy Thanksgiving to everyone. And although it's a holiday, it's also a workday for the Texans . They have practice on Thursday, and Texans coach DeMeco Ryans has warned the guys , and he means business.   There will be a weigh-in on Friday, so don't eat too much turkey, stuffing, sweet potatoes, pumpkin pie, pecan pie , apple pie, cherry pie—whatever. Don't overeat, because on Friday he's going to weigh these guys and see who's overeating, and you could get a fine if you eat too much.  Of course, another reason not to overeat is that it can make you sluggish before the all-important game on Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens here, starting at twelve o'clock sharp—a big game that the Texans must win. And a lot of this week, like every Thanksgiving, is about trying to cope with the holiday, family, and balancing things, just like all of you and I have. I also have a family and Thanksgiving. At the same time, I still have work to do, and the Texans have a tough job ahead of them against the Ravens.  Despite their record, despite their losing streak, they are still a capable team, and the Texans have already proven that they can't take anyone lightly, not with a four-six record, not after a zero-four start.  So we'll talk a lot about intangibles, but we'll also discuss the major injury news. It's tempting to delve into all of this, and the Texans are still hoping to get some injured players back on the practice field. We'll look at everything and talk a lot about it, you know, it's human nature to look ahead, especially when the door is wide open. But the Texans just played their most complete game of the season.  They crushed the Indianapolis Colts 26-3, a dominant victory. Meanwhile, the teams ahead of them in the AFC are floundering, and everyone is caught up in the absolutely insane quarterback drama with the Pittsburgh Steelers after Aaron Rodgers was benched and he lashed out at Mike McCarthy with fat-shaming accusations, ice cream sandwich talk, and claims that he snores in training camp. Oh my god, man, a lot of slander from Aaron Rodgers.  It seems that all this is true , but this does not mean at all that it was necessary to take the garbage out of the house.  As adults, they should have found common ground after so many years of working together.   A very disappointing finale for Aaron Rodgers, and he was fired from the Steelers, and the Texans play the Steelers and Mason Rudolph in a couple of weeks.  So we'll have plenty of time on Steelers week. We're focused on Ravens week, and if you're a Texan, don't get too hung up on the scoreboard. This is perfectly fine for the media and fans , but if you're a football player or Demeco Ryans, you shouldn't do this.
