But even if you lose this game, if you're the 49ers with your backup quarterback, what I'm assuming, but we'll we'll we'll finish up that thought in a little bit. Even if Mac Jones starts and you lose, you remain two loss column games ahead of the Seattle Seahawks. Two losses, Seattle will still have four. You can effectively seal the division with a win if you are the 49ers. Now, if you want to look at the conference standings, the 49ers, the one seed. Chicago is one loss column game behind the 49ers. So with a loss, the Bears and the 49ers are both at nine and two. The one seed is very very important, but this illustrates why it's been so important for the 49ers to rack up the wins that they've racked up so far this season. You have cushion here. The Bears are still going to play some tough games. They've got Buffalo, they have Jacksonville. They have to play Detroit again. I think the Bears, especially after giving up 250 rushing yards, I still think that Chicago has at least a couple losses in them. So the the 49ers are in a spot right now where they've earned a cushion where they don't have to win every single game to still have a very very good shot, if not a likely shot at the number one seed. Rams, by the way, in the postseason finally after that win. The Rams impress me because of their balance, but they don't have explosiveness and I don't think explosiveness is going to come back without Puka Nacua. Now, Davante Adams might be back, but he's not really as explosive of a receiver as he was before. The Rams are on the schedule for the 49ers. And of course, the Seahawks are on the schedule as well coming up on Sunday, and Seattle also fighting for their playoff lives at this point in the season. So as you can tell, for the 49ers, they're in a good spot. They've earned this spot. They've bought the depth on this football team. They've managed it properly to where they can absorb a Purdy absence. Now we'll see if he indeed is absent. After this Thanksgiving day, I'll be back at the team facility and we'll see exactly where the 49ers are. If it's Mac Jones starting on Sunday, I would handicap this as a toss-up between the 49ers and the Seahawks and a good opportunity for Mac to work with the 49ers set of weapons offensively, a good opportunity for the 49ers to play with some house money, some true house money if Purdy's not out there. And maybe an opportunity if Purdy isn't out there to give Brock the necessary rest so he can be a full capacity to chase this MVP down the stretch of the season. I think the last thing you would want as the 49ers is Purdy to go out there on a bum ankle in the rain against a really good defense, further injure himself, and also you know, lose efficiency because he's not playing at 100% or close to 100%, lose the efficiency that has put him in the driver's seat of the MVP award. I mean, it's all connected, right? The individual awards and team success. 49ers have to do what's best for the team and it was best to keep Mac Jones and now they might need Mac Jones moving forward. Happy Thanksgiving to everyone. I'm sure that you're eating dinner as this video is posted, but on all days I have to make sure to keep you apprised of what's happening around the 49ers. Looking back, looking forward to being back in that team facility tomorrow. There is never a dull moment with these 49ers who are nine and one, looking strong, but may have to tap into that quarterback depth in this massive massive week against the Seattle Seahawks.

title: 49ers BREAKING: Brock Purdy injury | TON of news...
text: Look where we are, back in front of the helmet for what might be the busiest 49ers update ever. Brock Purdy had some good news in Mexico. >> Yes, I got my tacos. >> But he did not practice today. An ankle issue which led to the taping of that ankle in the second quarter of the 49ers win against the Minnesota Vikings has Purdy day today. Now not convinced that this is a serious injury. It's not a high ankle sprain, but it's a good thing that the 49ers have Mac Jones. A good thing they didn't listen to all those armchair GMs on X saying they should trade Mac Jones. They play the Seattle Seahawks this weekend and even if you don't need Brock Purdy this weekend, there's a chance that you're going to need Mac to help you get a win at some point and he can help bridge the gap to the number one seed and the number one seed means an astronomically higher chance of winning the Super Bowl. So we'll keep our eyes on that. A big new roof that I reported on yesterday is out on the 49ers practice field, but it is sunny today in Santa Clara. So the 49ers do not need to use it quite yet. Other 49ers transactions, Brandon Cooks is indeed back and he really announced his return to the 49ers in a way that only a pilot can do. He flew over Levi Stadium landing at San Jose Airport and posted about it. But Brandon Cooks only temporarily gone from the 49ers. He has resigned to the practice squad. They did release Robert Beal Jr. the edge rusher yesterday to make room for Cooks. Austin Pleasant, the offensive lineman, has had his practice window opened. Pleasants worked at both guard and tackle over the course of training camp, but obviously now with the injury to Colton McKivitz, Austin Pleasants is going to working at tackle for the 49ers. And Nate Hobbs, defensive back, today was the final day to activate him from injured reserve. Day 21 of his practice window and the 49ers did activate Nate Hobbs from injured reserve. Colton McKivitz did go to IR to make room for that. And McKivitz's replacement is going to be Vederian Low, who missed all of training camp all but the very start of it, suffered a high ankle sprain on practice one. But the plan was to get him work at both left tackle and right tackle and they've been getting him weekly work at left tackle because Trent Williams never practices on Wednesdays. So he actually has some rapport with the starters. Vederian Low does. That I think that's really important. George Kittle pointed to that today. He's going to be moving over to the right side now to replace Colton McKivitz. >> Uh I'm definitely, you know, just going out there to just focus on doing my job. You know, Colton has, you know, had a great year. Um he's had a great year so far and um you know, it's a real shame that it was happened to him and I just want to go out there and honor him and um you know, just play great. I want to, you know, I want him to be proud. Um that's the most important thing. You know, I'm going to be, you know, asking him, you know, what is he seeing from me and you know, if he has anything for me that I can work on um throughout the rest of the season. But um at the end of the day, man, you know, like I said, he's established a a great, you know, culture around here. He's a he's a he's a tone setter. And um you know, I just want to make sure that I'm honoring him um and and playing up to that standard that he set for sure. >> Also no practice for Saran Neal, 49ers special teams ace and defensive back. Jordan Watkins, who's dealing with a groin issue, that is new for the 49ers, the receiver Watkins out. And no practice for Mike Evans today, but we are not expecting him to practice on Wednesday for the rest of the season. That's how they're going to be managed managing that Achilles tendonitis. And I'll tell you, I saw Mike Evans in that 49ers locker room and he that's good news because in weeks that Mike Evans has not played this year. We haven't seen him on Wednesday in the locker room. We'll put it that way. But weeks that he has played, he's in there and obviously played really well and took care of a lot of that Achilles tendonitis, but it is something that can continue to pop up, so you have to manage it properly if you're the 49ers and we'll see how they continue to manage it. Now speaking of managing injuries, rehab, saw Sam Okunlola for the first time since he broke his foot right before the 49ers flew out to Australia. 49ers defensive end was in the locker room. He was in good spirits, was walking without a limp. Remember Kyle Shanahan had said months ago that they hope to get Sam back for the end of this season and I think Sam Okunlola is on track to give the 49ers defensive line a nice reinforcement down the stretch of this season. Also talked to Nick Bosa in the 49ers locker room today and Nick obviously we have already discussed this a couple times, but this was his first chance to speak publicly about it. He didn't mean any harm with his comments about the fans in Mexico City were great in support of the 49ers on Sunday night against the Vikings. That was really clear to anyone who can process with their brain, but Nick Bosa was able to emphasize that perhaps social media is not real life. >> All the interactions that I had face to face were amazing, so. >> I just chew on that for a bit. The internet is not real life. I, you know, just as an aside, nobody has ever come up and said anything negative to me in person and I think that we can use that as a lesson between what Nick Bosa said and my experience, you can use that as a lesson that the discourse and the negativity and you know some of the lies that you hear online are not reflective of what is actually happening in the world. I digress. What's actually happening is the 49ers defense made a lot of progress against the Minnesota Vikings, especially from a cohesion standpoint up front along the defensive line. And of course the back end played well off of that. Javon Brown saw Kirk Cousins 2 weeks prior with the Raiders and basically at the time when that happened, he picked up on some tendencies, some clues from Kirk Cousins. And that's how he was able to step in front of his pass for pick six. But it was Deommodore Lenoir who pushed the left guard back into Kirk's lap who allowed that play to happen from Kirk Cousins, who coaxed that mistake. And Buckner has been working with some of the 49ers young defensive linemen, notably Michael Williams, after hours away from the team facility. And that is something that I think helps the 49ers rush with more cohesion and generally improve as the season progresses. >> I think those guys are always searching for edges. And when you're talking about a guy like Deommodore Lenoir who's been in the league so long and you're talking about Michael I mean that that just lets me know he's following the right people. You know when you got guys that do extra things or whatever requires to go out there and be the best version of themselves, I'm always going to be supportive of that. You know I'm sure they communicate that at a much higher level with Kris Kocurek or you know their D-line coaches, whether it be Scrubs or Cam and any of those type of guys. But for me it's just they're searching for the edge, you know. I don't they don't judge me on how much tape I watch. They they just I don't just watch it with them. So like let those guys go out there and try to find out what their edges are, you know what their extra motivation is to go out themselves. They're great. >> Now speaking of the defense and the safeties, look where Malik Mustafa is in terms of his coverage performance. Elite, a lot like Brock Purdy. Now remember Mustafa is a rookie in 2024, 0.12 yards allowed per cover snap, which is one of the best numbers we had ever seen, and ranked number one in the NFL. Unfortunately, he tore his ACL final game of that season, so 2025 wasn't as good. But Kyle Shanahan thinks that the 49ers have the best group of safeties in the league, and they're actually rotating them because they have Jair Brown with the pick six, they have Mustafa with these ridiculous numbers, and they have a promising young player named Marquis Seagal. So three players rotating at safety, and here's why. >> I think the guys have earned that. You know, I think we started the season, and obviously, you know, Six was on on on was hurt, and we went out there, and Six got a chance to play, and so did Tig, and those guys went out there and played well. But, you know, what we had seen in training camp, what we had seen in off-season program, you know, obviously Six didn't go through a lot of that, but we've seen guys that were competing at a very high level. And then we found a way to rotate those guys in there and get them all out there, you know, when he did come back, and he really showed up in a big way and played really well, and he continued it. Then obviously, for us, you know, Seagal went down, and he missed a couple games, and now Six is back, and he's got a chance to go back out there and really prove himself again, and right away I told those guys, the hot man will play. And I I enjoy it cuz it keeps the competitive fire going in all of those guys, and they love each other, and they cheer for each other, and they want each other to do well, and they are team-oriented guys that want to go out there and win, and they're finding ways to help us win um a lot, you know, and it's and it's been fun. We had a couple three safety packages out there for those guys, so it's pretty cool. >> Promise this would be a busy busy update. Brandon Aiyuk has signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad, and Kyle Shanahan continues to stay away from any emotional connection to that situation. It's been a long long time since Kyle Shanahan officially gave up on that, and Aiyuk finally did what he had to do to get released, and now he's with Adam Peters, the former 49ers executive who is the GM in Washington. A hell of a receiver room there, could be combustible with Stefon Diggs and Brandon Aiyuk both in it, but Kyle Shanahan basically said it's just a transaction to me. Washington got a good player and that's it. And you speak about combustible situations, obviously what happened in Pittsburgh today and yesterday and what's been happening at Pittsburgh, it sounds like according to what Aaron Rodgers said on the Pat McAfee show, off the chain crazy. He accused Mike McCarthy, the head coach of falling asleep during meetings and saying breaking down the huddle by saying 1 2 3 Packers instead of Steelers, saying that McCarthy is unfit to coach. Rodgers has been released by Pittsburgh and I'll just say that there is no better reality show in the entire world than the National Football League. Moving forward, the 49ers play the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. It's going to be right here at Levi's Stadium. Rain in the forecast, but there was also rain in the forecast today and as you can see, it is completely sunny. You could spot the 49ers new practice roof behind me as well. I know that we were just out on that practice field, but that is what the roof does look like. The 49ers will have Mike Evans in this game. We We know that. We'll see if it's Mac Jones or Brock Purdy. I I would My gut tells me that Brock Purdy is going to be out there on Sunday, but you never know and you never know if you know if he's out there and he's not effective or you don't want him to hurt it worst and this is why you you have invested in the backup quarterback position, but Evans represents elite and I'm talking about first ballot Hall of Fame level play at the wide receiver position especially at this age. And then on the other side for the Seattle Seahawks, you've got Jackson Smith-Njigba and I think that it is poetically perfect that these two guys are tied at top the league in yards per route run, probably our best stat to measure quarterback-receiver efficiency. And we have never seen a receiver finish a season in yards per run with as high of a mark as both Evans and JSN have this year. They are literally tied at 3.81. An elite yards per route run number is three. These guys are at almost four. So this is going to be it's all we have a treat in front of us here at Levi's Stadium with Mike Evans and JSN both at 3.81 yards per route run entering Sunday. And now the the Seahawks are coming off the bye. The 49ers is talking to guys. They were exhausted coming home on Monday. It is not a favorable part of the schedule here. NFL gave the 49ers a tough break, but they're going to have to grit their teeth, show some toughness. Said that Brandon Cooks was back. Jordan Watkins missed practice. It's good that the 49ers have depth at wide receiver now that they didn't have just a couple weeks ago. I mean, Deommodore Lenoir was a healthy scratch this past game. So they are they're in a better spot the 49ers were are than they were before at receiver and we'll see who plays, see who doesn't. It's going to extend to quarterback as well against the Seahawks. More coming for sure. Buckle up. Here are interviews from the locker room. >> How did you feel on on Sunday? >> Felt good. Felt like I'm getting better every week. >> Were you surprised by the reception that you got in Mexico City? >> Uh no. Um I thought it was good. I definitely didn't mean any harm my comments, but the environment was amazing and like it was the last time we were there. >> You made the the heart symbol. Was that a signal that you know there weren't any ill intents with what what you said to them? >> the intentions were pure. >> And at least they were cheering when you were on the field. So >> Yeah. All the interactions that I had face to face were amazing. So >> When you look at the film from Sunday versus Dallas, did you notice an improvement from your position group? >> For sure. Yeah, I think as a group we played the run, pass, everything we're getting to the quarterback quicker and putting pressure on them. Um so yeah, I think we're sending. >> I know he plays on the other side of the ball, but just what was your reaction to Colton's injury and is there a message from this team of how they'll play for him for the rest of the season? >> Yeah, it was tough. Um he's the quintessential 49er player like came in late round pick, battled, got cut, and worked his way to to being one of the better players in the league and to lose him, it's it's going to be a collective effort to to make up for it, but um that's why you sign a a swing tackle like Vederian. Um so. >> What have you seen from Seattle's offense this year? >> Um I think I mean dangerous as ever. JSN is playing as good as anybody. Um I assume Sam will be back this week, so I mean it's a Super Bowl caliber team and they're off the bye, so definitely not taking them lightly. >> When you're not on the field, do you ever keep an eye on what Keenan Allen and Mike Evans are doing out there? >> Uh yeah, I mean uh it's hard not to. Um I've watched Keenan for a lot of years with Joey. Um so I always knew what he could do and uh and both of them together is it's a pretty lethal combination. >> And you guys don't have a game on Thanksgiving. Is there a typical routine that you have? Do you spend it with certain teammates or anything like that? some years I don't have anybody in town. Some this year I have probably 15 people in town, so uh I'll be busy with my family and friends this year, but in the past I've popped over to other people's houses and but now it's not a set thing. >> With those 15 people, is there one specific person that you're hoping is doing the cooking and things like that? >> My mom. She'll be doing the majority of it and then my aunt is a used to be a pastry chef, so she could handle that side of things. >> What >> she do well? >> Um, she's doing an apple cobbler. >> Do you allow yourself to have that? >> Uh, maybe a little bit. Yeah, keep it light. >> Apologies if you've been you've been asked this, but the the reaction you got in Mexico City, how did how did you kind of digest that and is there anything you would want to clarify >> I already talked about it. >> Flora said that it felt more like a win on Sunday in Mexico. >> Yeah. >> Would you assess For sure. I think when you give up 10 points is a lot different than 40. So, uh, we felt like we did our job and and earned that win with the team. >> So, okay. Hard not to get. >> It's tough. >> Yeah. Oh yeah, no, it's just I think it's that's that's Trent kind of makes up unk package and then you throw in Keenen and Mike. That's really Everything. >> How great is the unk package when you think about the unks that you guys have? >> Great question. [clears throat] [laughter] Um, I thoroughly enjoy it. I mean, when you like you're in the huddle, it's third down and you see like Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, Keenen Allen, Deebo, me, I'm like, God, this is going to be really fun. And then I just there's a ton of trust because you have a lot of guys who've played a lot of football and they've made a lot of plays. And so you just trust that they're going to get their job done, catch the football, and make a change. >> Were you guys aware on Sunday that uh Brock was dealing with an ankle injury during that second quarter? >> He's dealing with an ankle injury? Oh. Nope. >> What's to say about him that you didn't even realize? >> Uh, I hype up Brock enough. I've said enough nice things about him. He's playing at an awesome level. He's a competitor. He's going to play through things that none of us know about. That's what you that's that's an NFL football player. You play through things. >> This is going to be the first offensive line change you guys have had to do this year without Colton. Um, how does that impact the offense and and protecting quarterback Jimmy Jimmy Colton? >> Um, well one, losing Colton, I mean, that's super tough for us. He's a staple of this offense. Uh, his mindset, his dedication to his craft, everything about Colton, like he levels us up every single day. Um, so I'm going to miss the heck out of him. He's like my favorite person to sit next to in the huddle. Honestly, I feel like when I line up next to him, reminds me a lot of lining up next to Joe Staley. Just like my confidence and knowing what I have to do, our communication. So, that's going to really suck. But, you know, I think Velo's done a really good job of being ready for his opportunities. You know, Trent doesn't practice on Wednesdays the whole season, so he's got a ton of reps with the first team on Wednesdays. So, I think he's going to step in nicely. I it's, you know, hard to replace a tackle like Page who's been in the system for so long, but you know, I think we'll try to do our best to adapt and we'll help out Velo in any way that he needs. But, yeah, I mean, Seattle's defense is always a challenge. So, they're fantastic and we're going to really have to protect that quarterback. >> How big is playing great against Dallas and against Cowboys, Cowboys in Dallas? And you come out, you have a very good game against the Minnesota Vikings. Then you come back and welcome the Seahawks to Levi's. With that high play that you guys have had on the offensive end, is there any extra excitement coming into this matchup given that it's the Seahawks or is this everyday game and it's another week? >> Um, I mean, it's a division game. That's how I view it. You know, it's Seahawks week. Um, they're a really good team. Best defense in the NFL besides the Vikings. They do everything really well. Nothing gets by them by their secondary. They're super physical. So, I mean, it's not like, you know, oh my gosh, it's the Seahawks. It's just, hey, it's another NFL game, but it's another fantastic team who's going to do everything they can to beat us. And I know that they don't want to lose, you know, another game to us and be full games back. So, it's going to be a grinder of a game. >> Was the see Mike Evans coming with that the the one hand catch for the touchdown in the last game but be back in time for the very matchup that he was really great in earlier this season? Does that change anything or no? >> If compared to him not being available obviously. >> Oh, I mean, when Mike plays, our offense is different [snorts] cuz you just have a guy that it's really hard to one-on-one him, so it changes what they have to do on defense. And if you don't have him, uh, you know, they can do a lot more. So, anytime Mike Evans plays, makes my job a lot easier. So, I love having Mike out there. >> Does Keenan bring a a similar level put similar level of stress on the defense or is it different from Mike? Like, how would you his impact? >> Um, I think it is similar. Uh, you know, you have a you have a very crafty guy, um, who can run any route that you want him to run. And I think the longer he's here, the more he's going to pick up the offense. Like he had a couple awesome conversions for us in Mexico City and in Dallas. So, uh, when you have both those guys out there, I think it's just you have to really focus on them. And so hopefully that just opens up a ton of stuff for me, Christian, and Deebo. >> Has [snorts] any of Christian's psychotic tendencies rubbed off on you in terms of your approach or offseason stuff or anything like that? >> Um, yes and no. I mean, one thing I love about Christian is I'm a guy who like who I take a shotgun approach to like everything. I try everything and then I see what I like and what I don't like like rehab wise, training wise, and then I narrow it down to see for the things that work best for me. And I think he's pretty similar to that. So when we can sit down there and you know bounce ideas off each other like we went to Germany together this offseason, that was really fun. But when you can sit down there and bounce ideas off each other because you're both a little um, a little out there in the head. Um, respectfully. Um, and it's just like you can just get new ideas and you can find things that you've never even heard of. >> And what did you guys do in Germany this offseason? >> Uh, you can ask him. It's a surprise. >> What do you like more, pancake blocking a guy or running over two guys into the end zone? Were they equal? >> Well, you know, I I think they're pretty equal. I used to say pancake block, but you know, touchdowns are really good for new contracts. So touchdowns are great. Um, but yeah, anytime that you put a defender on his back, it's it's a one-on-one moment. >> What's your typical Thanksgiving routine? my job is to play football. So like I'm not really like I love the holidays, but I have too many people here that are counting on me to be my best every single day. So eat a good dinner, go to bed at a great time, and I'll see you at work on Friday. >> No cheat meals? >> I mean, >> you guys? >> I had to eat calories. So I don't like I'm not going to eat you know an entire pie to myself, or I might. I don't know. But uh, probably just you know consume a lot of calories and get sleep. >> All right, thanks George. >> Thanks. >> plan I guess coming in to to be more at left or or where they going to try to get you working both? >> Yeah, I mean, be more on left for sure. you know, I always knew I was going to be a swing, you know, coming here. Um, definitely I get the majority of my work at left. Um, a lot of it. Um, but, you know, I always work on right as well. So, uh, that way I was just ready for whatever and, you know, ready for a moment like that. >> Mike scored the touchdown on the drive where Colton got hurt and you came in and and he said after that it was really important to you guys to score on that drive. Uh, could you just take me back through the moment you came in, the mentality, and how how it all got settled down? >> Yeah, definitely. Um, it was a lot of nerves for sure, you know, just because of one, you know, Colton is super tough guy and just see him down like that and just to see the reaction for all my teammates and everything. Um, I knew, first of all, every game means a lot to Colton and Colton means a lot to his team and I want to make sure I do right by him, you know, going out there and performing, you know, to the standard that he set. He set a really high standard here and, um, I want to make sure that I did that. Um, you know, just honestly just going out there, that first drive was a blur to me and I was just trying to, you know, get my rhythm, um, call my mental, and, you know, just kind of find my flow of the game. Um, but yeah, it was just it was really important, you know, for me personally to go on there, get that score, kind of settle in, um, and give myself time, you know, to go out there and execute. >> Now, Minnesota, they're kind of famously complex with the blitzes that seems like maybe the the toughest kind of game to be thrown right into. Uh, what do you credit for for being prepared for all the exotic looks they do throw at you? >> Yeah, definitely our coaches have for sure. You know, they had a plan throughout their entire week and, you know, it helped being in Colorado. You know, you had a lot of time to get in your playbook. You know, there was no reason to not know, you know, the game plan and our protection system and everything. So, you know, definitely our coaches have done a great job for us right. >> [laughter] >> Yeah, you mentioned as right going out Colton just has this awesome and, I think, your first was a a pancake. Was that like I know he's You probably remember that pancake. I mean, did you was that like in any way like, okay, you know, I'm going to be not that you were like in there freaking out, but like calming and like okay, you know, I'm in the game now. Like I said, man, honestly, I didn't I was just trying to find mental stability in a sense, you know, like I I went in there the game is already in the swing. We're trying to go and make a good drive. We're trying to score. We're trying to extend our lead. And I'm trying to make sure I go in there and I, you know, do my job. So I really wasn't able to kind of mentally settle in until after I have time at that time to kind of, you know, take a second to breathe, think about it and everything like that. But but yeah, man, I was just trying to go out there and do my job. That's pretty much it for me. Then you got to I mean, obviously tackles are hard to come by in the NFL. >> Um I don't know. You got a nice contract to come here. >> Did you feel like you know, maybe it's a stupid question, but um there was a respect level that they appreciated, you know, what you had put on tape throughout your career before you got here? >> Yeah, most definitely. You know, I knew, you know, what I was getting myself into coming here. I knew that, you know, when my number was going to be called, you know, that I would need to come through. And that's what they expected of me. And that's what I expected of myself most importantly. You know, I hold myself to a very high standard. And you know, I knew when it was my time and it would come that I would be ready and I want to be ready. And I want to just show my teammates and my coaches, you know, I have the utmost respect for everybody in this organization. It's a very tough organization to play for, but it's also very rewarding. You know, with the standard that, you know, coach sets, we have a ton of good players here. I have the respect for everybody. So I want I knew coming here I when my number was called, I was going to make sure that, you know, I put my best foot forward for sure. >> Why why is it tough to play here? >> We play hard. It's it's a it's a very it's a tough system, but it's a great system, you know, to learn. I feel like we have [music] so many good players. Everybody is expected to do their best every single day, you know. And when you got players like Fred, Trent, C-Mac, Kittle, like Brock, like you have all these guys, you have so many good players, you know you can win. If you can win in the Sunday. And you know having those guys, you know on our team it means everything to me and I just want to give those guys the best opportunity to win. You know I feel like the only thing you know this organization has done recently is win the big one. You know win the bowl. So you know me coming here I knew when my number was called I wanted to be a part of that and that's all I'm trying to do. >> You you mentioned Trent. What were your impressions of this O-line group before you got here and what's it been like kind of fitting in with with this group? >> Um I knew it was a veteran group you know with Trent Colton and then Brenda as well. Everyone is talking about Aaron Rodgers , it's just complete madness.  And I asked this question. Even if he said "one, two, three, Steelers," is that really what they do when they leave the meeting?  This is so high school level that I couldn't even believe it was actually happening.  But, I mean , it's terrible.  How did this team even get six wins?  This is the craziest thing. Well, I mean, if that was typical of McCarthy throughout his tenure, he won a lot of games, even with the Cowboys.  I mean, he won a lot of games there.  They just fell a little short in the playoffs. Yeah, it's just...we've never heard of it getting to the point where he was sleeping in meetings and not even watching the game replays. It seems Rogers was saying he should stop choosing combinations, and he didn't want to give it up. Ugh. And eventually his...I mean, this story just gets weirder and weirder.  And now Aaron Rodgers has been fired.  By the way , you wrote an article, I think, for the Philly Voice.  Were you the one who wrote the article about whether the Eagles really ended Aaron Rodgers' career?   That's exactly what they did.  Look, no matter what they said about McCarthy, Rodgers and everything else, when they won, nobody paid attention. You just watched the games and sometimes you saw Aaron Rodgers yelling at McCarthy on the sideline, but they were winning. That defeat, their second in a row, apparently changed everything for the Steelers. It was, "Oh my God, I can't believe we lost to the Eagles, huh?" We lost...if you're for the Steelers, you won in time of possession, in total yards, in third downs, but you lost the game. So it seemed like it had all reached a boiling point. So the Steelers' loss really changed everything about their season. And then Aaron Rodgers—ironically, to Mike— if this is the last pass of his NFL career, it was against the team he beat first in the playoffs and against the organization he was winning with. So, at that moment, everything came full circle .  Oh, by the way, his last pass will be remembered as a touchdown to a Division III guy who played at Colgate and was originally from Pennsylvania. Well, that's also crazy.  I mean, he was a bit passive-aggressive against management, as if to say: we told you this guy should be in the game, and you didn't listen to us.  So I hope the people up there take note of how to run a football team— that's essentially what he said.  Listen , this all got really confusing, and it was happening around 11pm. And it all happened exactly like that.  It was all pretty crazy.   It'll be even crazier when Rodgers becomes head coach next week, after McCarthy is fired.   Do you think, Moshe, he will eventually play for some team at the finish line, for example, for the Patriots? Some have hinted at this because Baltimore plays Pittsburgh twice at the end of the season, and in the AFC, a wild card spot can still be won .  I mean, if you're New England or Baltimore, I know you have a negative record, but if you had a better quarterback, do we think we've seen the last of Aaron Rodgers? I think so.  I really think so .  Even if you're Baltimore or Arizona , if someone needs you as a quarterback , New England, do you really watch the game tape and think Aaron Rodgers is going to be the deciding factor for you? Besides, you know, if you don't make this guy happy, what will he say about you on the Pat McAfee show? I saw this meme, it's kind of funny, but true: that interview was like the media version of Antonio Brown leaving the Bucks, right? Like, just take off your shirt right in the stadium and just... Get out of here.  Yes. Yes.  Yes, yes. But that was probably the final nail in the coffin, I think. Jeff, lost season this Thanksgiving.  What interesting stories there are, because there is something to see here.  You have a worthless Eagles offense against a worthless Dallas defense. Who will win this battle of wits? This is a very, very valid question.  Um, the Eagles were hoping to get a little more energy last week with the return of Barkley and Devonta Smith. Devonta Smith got 12 targets, and the most interesting thing is that Milton only had 21 pass attempts, so he was clearly looking for him, but it didn't work. Aside from the first quarter, they didn't create a single explosive play.  Now, on the other hand, the Cowboys find themselves in the same situation.  They are playing terribly and are hoping that the return of a few players, like Jerry Porter Jr. , will help;  it looks like Jaylen Thompson, the safety they signed as a free agent, will be able to play. And if you look at their defense, you might think: now that Kobe Duran is healthy, Porter is healthy, Jaylen Thompson is ready to come back, it could help them play nickel defense. We can have a little bumpy ending here and that'll be quite all right. >> I got one more for you. Producer Mark just gave me in my ear, and it's the Green Bay Packers. What if he goes back to Green Bay, maybe just sits on the bench and just retires as a Packer? What what's the likelihood we could see that? >> So that's the storybook ending, right? I do think that there's something to be said for yes, this whole Pittsburgh Steelers ending ended in a blaze. It was absolutely insane what we saw on Wednesday and how all of this went down. If you want a little bit more of a storybook ending for [music] Aaron Rogers, wouldn't be that crazy if all of a sudden he goes back to where it all started at Lambeau Field with the Green Bay Packers. Of course, [music] he's not going to be the starter. That belongs to Jordan Love, but you can go back to the organization where you hoisted a Lombardi trophy, etched your Hall of Fame resume, and be a quasi offensive coordinator, work with Jordan Love, and in the worst case scenario ala Bo Nix in the playoffs last year, you're the Green Bay Packers, you're not turning to a Jared Stidham, you're turning to Aaron Rogers. Again, you don't want that to happen, but the insurance policy of a franchise legend behind your starting quarterback, that would be very attractive, I would imagine, to the Green Bay Packers. And for Aaron Rogers, it would be a homecoming that I think he would embrace. Again, is he okay with being a backup? Does he want to start? Those are all questions that only Aaron Rogers can answer, but from the outside looking in, if we're not talking about a grudge match between the Baltimore Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers, I kind of like this one the best. >> So many storylines to follow here between where Rogers is going to end up, what happens to the Steelers organization, what happens to Mike McCarthy. So much to unpack here. Tyler, really appreciate your insight today, my friend. And taking one more look at the top landing spots for Rogers according to Tyler, Patriots, Ravens, Cardinals. He could retire or maybe reunite in Green Bay and then retire as a Packer for story book ending.

title: Daboll, Fassel & Bradley on Red Zone Details, Joey Slye's Pro Bowl Case & the Rematch | Titans
text: As far as increasing performance for you, in terms of points scored, I know you still want to complete more of those drives. Certainly.  This is the main goal of the game.  Take care of the ball and score points. So, you know, the last few weeks we've started to put a little more emphasis on working in the red zone and on third downs on Wednesdays. We do it on Thursday, we do it on Friday.  First drive, we're moving forward, third and 12 at the 20-yard line , you know, it's a pretty tough situation. I had to throw the ball away.  At the end of the half , I would have liked another rally, but I had to stop the clock and just score points.  We wanted to take as much time as possible to not give the ball to them, but at the same time complete the drive. And then we had a fumble there. So everyone needs to work hard: both coaches and players, continuing to focus on these situations. What are the subtleties you are trying to improve in your red zone offense, if there are any problems ? I think you just have to do your job.  If you have a short five-yard pass, you have to make that play , just make it.  If there is a certain reading of the game depending on the safety, we have to implement it.  We must do well in the task of moving forward.  You know, we had a bad takeout on that drive-thru.  You need to stay in the game and keep moving the ball forward.  Of course, you'd like to make big plays in the end zone, but if they're blocked, the space narrows , the timing becomes faster, the passing windows are narrower, and there are more defenders.  It's simply a game in a limited space where every detail is crucial. How many times have you had situations where you played the same team twice in three weeks, and what's the difficulty in that?   I'm sure there were. I've been in this business for a long time, but every time you spend a lot of time preparing, watching all the available video material. And then you immediately see a lot of the same thing .  Of course, they have our match and the game they just played against the Giants .  But it is important to be as focused on the details as possible.  You will be watching the match they just played against New York.  You will carefully analyze your game records, what you did, and what they opposed you.  But, as a professional, to be on top of things in training, again, you can look back at the cuts you made the week before, and the guys are like: yeah, we've seen that before.  So let's just keep emphasizing the details. Considering they were mostly good at avoiding secs, what happened in the game against the Cowboys that threw them off track a bit? They have good players.  We knew it would be difficult to block these inside players .  They had, I think, five shutouts against Arizona at home and then five shutouts against the Forty-Niners.  You know, in a few cases they destroyed the envelope , and some Cam could have easily avoided. So, secy is a team effort. Offensive line, receivers, quarterback, but when you can avoid them at the quarterback position , that's what you should try to do . Apart from perhaps his performance on the field, what has impressed you about Tony Pollard and the way he conducts his business?   I can't say enough good things about Tony.   A true professional in every sense of the word on the field, as a leader and as a player. Obviously, his performance speaks for itself off the field—as a husband, as a father.  Just a wonderful person.  Does everything right, exactly the way you want him to do it.  He's a great example for the whole team in how he approaches, I would say, not only being in the building as a professional athlete, but also as a person. If running the ball, as Robert said earlier, is the most effective way to be successful in the red zone, what exactly is stopping you from doing so?  I mean, I think sometimes we run the ball well and sometimes we don't.  Again, the field is narrowing there.  You need to put player against player and move the ball forward well.  But again, whether you're running or passing, it's a limited-space game and you have to be precise.  Whether it's drop timing, route details, or the power blocks you need to perform there. This is a game that requires attention to detail in that area.  These are very tight conditions. Um, this is, I would say, a more difficult part of the game than when you have a lot of space.  So we continue to do this every day.  We will continue to do this every day, but it really makes a huge difference in many games.  You know, the red zone game—you get there, look at last week, like Jacksonville vs. the Giants, how many times they got there and the outcome of that game—that's a huge part of it. What were you thinking as you watched Cam's final touchdown?  Was this one of those “no, no, no, no—great game” moments? Um, no, I mean, this is obviously a pretty impressive moment.  Um, you know, it was late in the game, and if he's going to do everything he can to give us a chance late in the game, then if there's an interception—whether it's an interception on the last play or whatever it was.  So, um, you know, we would like it to be in a more tense situation.  Um, you know , you have to make sure you're handling the ball wisely. How do you like Tate's game in his second, as they say, philosophically changed attack? Yeah, I mean, Tate is smart.  Um, we've already played what we call it, relative to being on the ball at times, we did it during camp, he did it.  Um, we did a little more, but he's real, Tate—a pro. He's smart, he's played a lot of positions, moving around the field, and it's, um, no wonder how he takes it all. Going back to the takeaway game, everyone has a lot of the same plays in attack, how much harder has it become this season to take the ball away when you see so many defensive schemes with a lot of players on the line? It is always, truly always a challenge.  Um, and every team you play has its own structure.  The team we're going to play, they offer a variety of schemes.  Um, it all starts from the center, with Shloti, who organizes everything and distributes people as we need them Um, but then again, you know, if you're playing against a front four, you know where they are.  It's a little different when they're scattered everywhere.  I think most teams do a variety of things.  It's, you know, whether you're running or throwing the ball, it's tough in this league.  You must be very focused on details and perform your work efficiently.   A big special teams player, uh, before , and you, like...what were your first conversations with him like? Excuse me, who are you talking about? Uh, Corey Thornton. Oh, yes.  Um, just got a chance to meet him for the first time today. Booker T. Washington High School in Miami .  I remember recruiting players there in 2001 when I was a limited-funds coach at Bucknell University.  So we got a little nostalgic for a few minutes, and I took the running back from there to Bucknell. That's how it was, but I know he's been in the league for a year and a half, and I don't know much about him, but enough to say he looks like a player who can play football.  So I'm looking forward to meeting him. I know as a team you would like to finish a lot of these attacks on offense, but how reliable has Joey been lately? Fantastic.  Yes, I think everyone sees that.  He's just a kicker with a powerful leg, extremely accurate. He is focused on everything.  His opening shots got much better. So, like I said last week, I think he's probably the most underrated kicker in the league, in my opinion, because there are a lot of very worthy and recognized kickers. And Joey was kind of a wanderer who finally found his home, and I think he was fantastic. And I think it's never too early to say he should be a Pro Bowl kicker for the AFC .  I know there are a lot of very good players.  You know, Cincinnati, Jacksonville , a lot of good ones, but I mean, you have to put Joey in the same league as them .  You must. He talked about being a wanderer and then finding a home here with you. What exactly worked so well between you two? When we first signed him, I remember calling him because I competed against him and knew him, not personally, but I remember us spending over an hour on the phone.  And before we signed him, he finished a year in New England, and I opened up all, I think he had about 28 attempts, and I said, "I have the video in front of me."  I said, "Joey, I'll walk you through all 28 attempts, just tell me from memory about each shot, what you felt and how it went."  And he didn't have the video in front of him , but he remembered almost every shot : "Hey, that was a good shot."  It was nice, you know, I play a little bit right to left .  And it was an interesting conversation when we were talking about our kicker, like, " Yeah, let's give this guy a chance."  I think he's really good, and Borgonzi and the whole team seemed to feel the same way .  So it's not that we did anything, he's just very process-oriented and I think he's gotten a lot better at doing it without having to rethink the play or the shot. So he's just, uh, yeah, a "traveler" who deserves not to be one. So I'm proud of him for what he did to prove: he not only belongs in the NFL , but he's that guy for somebody, and you know, he's ours, and I'm happy about that. How important is the mental component for kickers, the technique, and you know, it's almost like taking a free throw for them. How deep does Joey go into this part, as far as you know? Very much. I am well-versed in all of this and he is very tech-oriented. While I just said that it's better not to overthink everything, there's also an element where you have to be mindful of things that set you up for the process of making a shot. And I think there's a balance here, and it balances very well between not being an overthinker and not falling into analysis paralysis, you know, but also not going out there without thinking about anything at all So it's a wonderful process—finding that "golden mean." He's very technique-oriented, and I think he's so tuned into it that it helps him stay on track. Yes. I know you invited players to carve pumpkins for Halloween. Do you invite the guys to Thanksgiving , those players who have nowhere else to go? Yes, we have a good company coming tomorrow , we just want to make sure everyone is taken care of.  Usually it ends up that our players, and we've learned this because we've been talking about it for the last few days, do a great job of inviting teammates home who are alone or with someone else.  And I think where I'm intervening, hopefully, is the guys that we've signed in the last few days or weeks, who are obviously here themselves.  Many of them live in a hotel nearby, so they have somewhere to go. So, everyone was taken care of, and I was like the last one left without a partner, one of those lonely guys.  So yes. But I've noticed that our guys are doing a great job of accepting their teammates, and that's really cool .   Do you always wear cleats to training? You noticed, huh?  Yes, I... Why are you wearing them? God, it was four or five years ago, and I know sometimes people think I just run around in sneakers because I want to appear unknown. For me, it's purely a tactical move because I'm on the field, moving around a lot during special teams practices, and when I'm without cleats, well, there are times when I slip or have to be careful to get out of the way in time.  So honestly, the boots give me a little bit better grip to move, step aside and be part of the game because I like to run right behind everyone and see what they see.  So the boots help me train better. What about you? Yes.  So it's not...we're not getting cleats for the "My Cause My Cleats" campaign.  These are training shoes.  I'll wear it on game day because I don't need boots during the match.  So I'll be wearing cleats to training on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday, and just regular shoes on Saturday and Sunday .  My cause, My Cleats, is Prison Fellowship Angel Tree, an organization we are hosting a summer camp for here in June.  This is a fantastic cause, an incredible organization, and the wonderful children who are a part of it.  So yeah, you know.  How are you, Juice?  Here, here is Juice.   That's it.  Aha.  I, I don't have any gloves.  Do you like what you see? Juice just...We have a " 500 Points Club" in special teams.  And last year, Juice became our "500 Points Club" champion. The first guy in my 18 years as a special teams coordinator to score 1,000 or more.  And last game, he just reached the 500-point mark in nine or ten games.  So let's see if we can get to 1000 again, Juice. Yes, I understand. Okay, dude. Okay, where to start?  Well, of course, we did n't play very well in last Sunday's match.  So, um, there are a lot of things we need to fix.  It wasn't a game we could be proud of or happy about.  But we had a good meeting.  There were, you know, quite frank conversations about this.  Part of that is because Dallas was a truly explosive team.  And sometimes you get what you focus on.  Hey, we have to neutralize these explosive moments.  That's how quickly they score, and we highlighted some things, and we did well, but we couldn't execute the rest.  And you know, the draw lasts quite a long time. So some of those short passes or throws to the wing—we sometimes went back too deep and couldn't cover those areas in time. And this whole story was about our defense in general.  Some of the things we emphasized were necessary, but other problems arose that hurt us. How disappointing is that?  Sorry. How frustrating is it when you try to press with seven players, the coverage breaks, you try to add pressure with a blitz, they don't get the quarterback, and nothing seems to work You finally start to feel the situation.  Sometimes you use blitz if you feel like the game is lacking energy and you say, "Okay, let's try it." Let's go blitz to add energy, you know, and stimulate the process—it happens all over the league.  So sometimes it's used like this: let's get them.  Now, you are right.  We tried to use pressure unconventionally, involving five players , pulling others away, creating different cover schemes that were understandable to us , but perhaps difficult for the opponent. But some of these schemes simply didn't work in time. Robert mentioned that the players in this game were a bit slow.  Why do you think this happened? Well, I think, as I said, sometimes their players' routes were very deep.  Some teams run 14-yard digs, and they run 18. Okay, let's go deeper so we can handle those digs if our main pressure doesn't work.  And if it's a short play, we just didn't see the speed in trying to get the ball as quickly as possible.  So that's the part, you know, sometimes we did well in the early stages, but after, you know, the first part of the game, the speed we just didn't see on the record.   Did you mention Corey Thornton? Uh, no, I don't know that much about him , you know, I'm glad he's with us, but, well, you know, we're studying, I'm studying him, you know. Is inviting someone from outside a certain signal for guys? Well, you know, it's, I mean, there are different moments, right?  Sometimes, you know, when guys are injured, you need a person for that position.  You know, guys always look at the locker room and feel that side of things, but, you know, you also try to create competition within your team. Twice in such a short time, you expect them to try to attack you with what made them successful the first time, right? Yeah, I think you look at it and say that even if it was an inaccurate pass, you saw that moment with the long shot into the end zone that he missed.  Uh, you know, things like, okay, let's make sure this doesn't happen again.  So not just the successful plays, but the overall pattern—you look at how they tried to attack us and say, okay, we have to fix that before we play them again.   Was it helpful to see, given, you know, where you are now defensively with all the struggles, to see Jacksonville just a few weeks ago?  This is ... Uh, yes, it's more like a recollection.  You know, I think you go back to that and say, hey, remember some of the things that they did that we were emphasizing, you know , here they are on the record, and they remember, you know, you see it coming back to their memory.  So this part is a little fresh in their memory after playing them two weeks ago. OK.  Thank you. Thank you.

text: After a tumultuous week in Pittsburgh, the Steelers are back in action at 3 PM [music] Eastern today hosting the Broncos. Now, let's get to Steelers owner Art Rooney said this. [music] Here's former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin who spent 19 seasons in Pittsburgh weighing in [music] on the situation. >> It's a dumpster fire and I don't say that in a judgmental way. I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. Um but but it it certainly um is upsetting and I'm sure uh still a nation is upset. He was beloved and I'm not overexaggerating that particularly from my perspective. I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process >> or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way. >> Mike T, as our former GM at the table, have we seen the last of Aaron Rogers? >> I don't think so. And you have one of the five best arguably quarterbacks of all time sitting at home who's in this like in shape unlike guys like Drew Brees and Philip Rivers from last year. DJ Unclelay is starting this week. >> Yeah. Yeah. Tommy Devito is starting this week. So to me, >> against each other. >> Yeah. Right. Right.
